e44bc2289b.why: LEAD FIX applied (2026-11-27): the re-checker's exact phrase. Re-checker's note: Both new wrong choices are wrong on the record, not just another view. Soares-Weiser said the review examined 'whether interventions to promote mask wearing help to slow the spread', and that it 'is not able to address the question of whether mask-wearing itself reduces people's risk of contracting or spreading respiratory viruses', which rules out 'keeps its wearer from passing illness on'. The trials compared a mask-promotion arm with a control arm (masks against no masks, F18), with no comparison against staying home. The key matches her words. Remaining problem: the context paraphrases her caveat inexactly. 'could not answer whether wearing a mask itself lowers a person's risk' drops 'of contracting or spreading', and the spreading half is exactly what makes the new 'passing illness on' choice wrong, so the card leaves that out. Exact fix: replace 'whether wearing a mask itself lowers a person's risk' with 'whether wearing a mask itself lowers a person's risk of catching or spreading illness'. 42.3 and 13.3 percent, 'inconclusive' and 'hampers drawing firm conclusions' are exact.

3a97dc84db.why: LEAD FIX applied (2026-11-27): the re-checker's exact phrase. Re-checker's note: Facts check out: 65 studies from 19 countries; at 40 weeks severe-disease protection was 90.2% (ancestral, alpha, delta) and 88.9% (BA.1), and reinfection protection was 36.1% for BA.1 and 78.6% for the earlier forms. The paper says 'protection from re-infection from all variants wanes over time', and that protection against severe disease 'remained high for all variants'. The context fix is right, and the four choices are coherent and distinct. 'What protection, if any' is neutral. Remaining problem, a standout key: every wrong choice now puts an absolute in the changing slot ('unchanged', 'gone', 'gone ... gone'), and the key alone is hedged ('falling'), the middle of the unchanged-falling-gone scale. A test-wise student who knows no immunology avoids the absolutes and lands on the key, the same tell the judge flagged in 'no fall at all', now in three choices. Exact fix: replace the choice 'Still high against severe illness, and unchanged against catching it again' with 'Falling against severe illness, as fast as against catching it again'. It is not absolute, and it is wrong on the record for every group: severe-disease protection 'remained high' and 'appears to be durable' while reinfection protection waned.

4ea65d608c.why: LEAD FIX applied (2026-11-27): the re-checker's exact phrase. Exact fix: replace 'Neither origin was likelier, on the evidence it had' with 'A jump from animals was likelier, held with moderate confidence', which completes a lab-or-animals by low-or-moderate grid and is wrong for the CIA. Minor and optional: Wray stated the FBI's judgement in February 2023, not its confidence level, which came from the 2021 assessment and later reports.
